title: Sort website visitors and book sales meetings automatically
summary: Agency Boldest built a website sales agent for software company Delectable; its co-founder says it sorts visitors by their questions and books meetings with promising buyers unaided.
agent_role: The agent answers visitor questions, sorts visitors into buyer types using a structured sales method, and books meetings for qualified leads. The sales team only takes the booked meetings.
outcome: Boldest's co-founder says the agent books qualified meetings without sales involvement. The interviewer notes no conversion figures were given.
what_they_did: The agency Boldest built a sales agent for the website of Delectable, a company that sells software to other businesses. The agent learned the product and a step-by-step sales method. It sorts visitors into buyer types based on the questions they ask. When a visitor looks like a real buyer, it books a meeting in the scheduling tool Calendly, with no salesperson involved.
how_it_went: Co-founder Keith Pires says promising visitors get meetings booked automatically. The interviewer, who reposted the account, notes that no numbers were shared. They would want to see how many meetings lead to real sales opportunities.
worth_knowing: All evidence so far is the founder's own account. Before trusting a setup like this, track how many booked meetings turn into real sales opportunities.
prompt: Act as the sales assistant on [company website] for [product]. Use [product docs] and this qualification method: [criteria, e.g. budget, authority, need, timeline]. Answer visitor questions, and classify each visitor as one of [buyer types] based on what they ask. When a visitor meets [qualification threshold], offer a meeting through [Calendly link]. Log each conversation with its buyer type and the reason for your decision in [spreadsheet]. Show me 10 sample conversations and your classifications for review before going live.

curation.rationale: A real deployed sales agent that qualifies website visitors and books Calendly meetings on its own. Evidence is only the founder's interview account, retold by a third party who notes there are no figures, and the post is largely event promotion.
